fields.description:
# S6 — Bounded concurrent gate executions, with fast-fail admission

## Why this story exists (added 2026-09-03 on operator input)

Operator: **~10 plan reviews run in parallel frequently**, plus code reviews and autodeploy contending for the same volume.

This invalidates an assumption the rest of the epic rests on. Option A caps each accumulator via a high-water-mark GC, and **a high-water-mark GC assumes evictable data exists.** Under ~10 concurrent gate runs it largely does not.

The mechanism is documented in the code itself. `src/rebar/_snapshot/janitor.py` relies on POSIX **delete-on-last-close** plus touch-on-read mtime recency, and deliberately takes **no per-reader lease** — a PID+heartbeat lease was spiked and REJECTED as unsound (N readers per entry, PID reuse, crash-stale leases), following Gitaly/Sourcegraph/Bazel/ccache. It also skips entries inside a grace window. So the janitor may UNLINK an in-flight snapshot, but the blocks are not returned until the last reader closes.

**Consequence: during peak concurrency the held bytes are live, not garbage.** A cap set below peak concurrent hold cannot be honoured — the GC runs, finds nothing evictable, and the volume fills anyway. Same shape as the failure this epic exists to fix: bug 3276 measured prune's reclaimable ceiling at ~1.06 GB against a 29 GB problem.

Without this story, S2-S5's caps are aspirational under exactly the load that causes the incident.

## Scope — operator-specified design

Both **plan-review** and **completion-verifier** executions create a copy of the repo at a specific ref, so both consume the bounded resource and **share one counter**.

**At capacity the call FAST-FAILS.** It does not queue and does not block. The caller receives a 'try again later' style response that names congestion as the cause, so an agent can back off and retry rather than hang or interpret it as a gate failure.

Fast-fail rather than queueing is deliberate: a queued gate still holds its thread and its resident memory while waiting, so a queue converts disk pressure into memory pressure. Given bug 9ea3 measured ~739 MB resident per complete plan-review, queueing ten of them is the OOM this epic is adjacent to. Shedding load is the correct primitive.

Design considerations to settle in implementation, not prescribed here:
- Gate work runs **in-process on a daemon thread** (`src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py` `_spawn_gate_daemon`), so an in-process counter covers MCP-driven gates — but **CLI gates run in separate processes**, so the counter must be cross-process (filesystem/lock-based) or the bound is partial. A bound covering one path is not a bound.
- The rejection must be DISTINGUISHABLE from a gate verdict. An agent must not read congestion as INDETERMINATE or as a failed review, or it will burn a retry budget or mis-record a result.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: a configurable limit bounds concurrent plan-review AND completion-verifier executions against ONE shared counter, with a default derived from measurement. Verified by a test that starts limit+1 executions and asserts the last is rejected while the others run.
- [ ] AC2: at capacity the call FAST-FAILS immediately — it does not block, queue, or wait. Verified by a test asserting the rejected call returns within a small bound rather than after a holder releases.
- [ ] AC3: the rejection is actionable and unambiguous — it names congestion, indicates the caller should retry later, and is distinguishable in type/shape from a gate verdict (not INDETERMINATE, not a FAIL). Verified by a test asserting the error shape over the MCP surface and the CLI.
- [ ] AC4: the bound covers BOTH the in-process MCP daemon path and separate-process CLI runs against the same counter. Verified by a test exercising each path.
- [ ] AC5: releasing is crash-safe — a gate process that dies does not permanently consume a slot. Verified by a test that kills a holder and asserts reclamation.
- [ ] AC6: the limit is a documented config key with a stated default and rationale, not a hardcoded constant. Verified by reading the config schema and docs/config.md.
- [ ] AC7: rejections publish a metric so congestion is visible rather than silent. Verified by a test asserting emission on a rejected admission.

## Testing

- `python -m pytest tests -k "gate_admission or concurrency" -q`
- `make lint && make typecheck` (a new config key trips the shrink-only mechanism ratchet; justify it in-tree with a `# mechanism-ok:` marker naming this ticket, never by editing the baseline)
- Contention shape: this composes a cross-process counter with gate execution, so route contention cases to the EXISTING shared suites per AGENTS.md rather than a bespoke harness.
fields.title: S6 — Fast-fail gate admission above a configurable concurrency cap
